messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: spike in 5xxs on /v1/embeddings (us-east-1). Error rate from 0.3% -> 9.7% in ~3m. Incident ID: inc-1965432100. Paging oncall: samir (oncall). 

samir (oncall): seeing it. digging into ingress and kernel logs. rolling back recent kv-ttl tunables?

jess (eng-sre): I'm on logs too. looks like a KV cache eviction storm after the TTL change rolled at 02:05. lots of KV misses -> model warmups -> memory pressure -> OOM-ish failures on several pods.

li (eng-runtime): confirming. the runtime observed rapid spike in repeated full-attention recompute for embeddings worker pool. latency 300ms -> 9s for some requests. fallback model kept retrying and hitting quota throttles.

nate (support): heads-up: I already saw 8 customer tickets in the last 10m complaining about 5xxs and timeouts. most are Dedicated customers. I linked inc-1965432100 to the ticket threads.

samir (oncall): mitigation: disabling the ttl reduction we deployed at 02:05, and enabling aggressive prefix/KV caching bypass for embeddings route to avoid recompute. applying now: 
```bash
# revert tunable
redwoodctl config set runtime.kv.ttl.default 3600 --release inc-1965432100
```

jess (eng-sre): applying canary first to us-east-1a. watching. also raising pod memory limits temporarily to avoid OOM restarts.

incident-bot: Deploy started by jess (eng-sre) for config rollback. CI run id: ci-90521.

samir (oncall): after the rollback: error rate dropped to ~1.1% in 90s, latency back to 85ms median. still seeing a handful of timeouts from inflight requests that retried.

maria (pm): customer impact assessment: which customers saw errors, and estimate of duration of impact? we need to categorize P0 vs P1 and decide postmortem scope.

nate (support): list copied: 
- enterprise-acme (dedicated) 02:06-02:10 ~500 failed requests
- shoply (hosted) 02:07-02:09 ~120 failed requests
- synthbio (dedicated) 02:05-02:12 ~1.2k failed/slow tokens
I filed individual customer follow-ups and added to CRM.

jess (eng-sre): impact summary: ~0.8% of global embeddings traffic impacted, but concentrated on Dedicated pools us-east. Single-customer degradation for synthbio is most severe. Recommend P1 incident (customer-impacted but mitigated within ~10m).

li (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: the TTL change lowered default KV TTL from 3600s -> 30s to try to reduce cold-kv ram. that created a stampede effect on high-QPS embedding prefixes because the runtime didn't progressively backoff warmups. Combined with a rolling retry loop in client library we saw amplified load.

samir (oncall): agree. until we close, I'll keep oncall watch for 1h and escalate if recurrence.

maria (pm): scheduling post-incident review: propose 1hr postmortem meeting today at 16:00 UTC. attendees: eng-runtime, eng-sre, support, product, and customer success. action item owners must be set during thread.

jess (eng-sre): I'll draft a short root-cause doc and attach histograms. estimated write-up time 2-3h.

li (eng-runtime): Action items I propose now: 
1) Add progressive backoff for KV warmups to avoid stampede. Owner: li. Sizing: 3-5d (design + test + rollout). Severity: P1 -> high priority for Q next sprint.
2) Add safety toggle to block aggressive TTL < 300s for high-QPS prefixes. Owner: jess. Sizing: 1d. Severity: P2 but quick win for this quarter.
3) Customer remediation runbook: proactive credit + email template for Dedicated customers. Owner: maria + nate. Sizing: 3-4h. Severity: P1 customer-facing.

maria (pm): I'll align customer comms with CS and legal. Tagging this for Q3 reliability initiatives as a targeted task: "KV warmup backoff".

nate (support): for synthbio we should offer a credits package and a technical postmortem call. I'll prepare draft and send to maria.

samir (oncall): operational followups: temporary autoscaler tweaks to reduce parallel warmup tasks. Owner: samir. Sizing: 0.5d to configure + 1h monitor. Severity: P1 ops.

jess (eng-sre): we should also add a monitoring alert for sudden TTL-related miss-rate deltas: create a delta metric for kv.miss_rate over 1m and 5m windows. Owner: jess. Sizing: 1d.

li (eng-runtime): I'll open a formal RFC for the backoff design. Link to RFC will be posted in the PM notes. Sizing in RFC: 3-5d engineering, plus 2d QA.

maria (pm): let's prioritize items by impact/time-to-fix: 
- P1 fast wins (<=1d): autoscaler tweak (samir), safety toggle block (jess), customer comms (maria+nate) -> schedule for this week.
- P1 larger (3-5d): KV warmup backoff (li) -> plan for next sprint and Q3 reliability work.
- P2 monitoring alerts (jess) -> can be slotted next-week.

samir (oncall): creating the action items in tracker now. I'll include estimates and link to this thread.

incident-bot: Action items created: AI-712 (autoscaler tweak) assigned samir, eta 1d; AI-713 (safety TTL guard) assigned jess, eta 1d; AI-714 (customer comms) assigned maria+nate, eta 8h; AI-715 (kv backoff design) assigned li, eta 5d; AI-716 (monitor delta alert) assigned jess, eta 1d.

jess (eng-sre): note: add post-deploy canary window and rollback playbook to AI-715.

li (eng-runtime): will include canary and load-tests in the RFC.

maria (pm): postmortem meeting confirmed 16:00 UTC today. Agenda: timeline, root cause, action items + owners + prioritization, customer comms. I'll create calendar invite and link RFC draft.

nate (support): I'll prep the synthbio briefing packet and the tickets for credits.

samir (oncall): leaving watch at 03:20 UTC. no further spikes in last 20m. handing off to next oncall.

jess (eng-sre): thanks everyone. I'll follow up in the postmortem doc with graphs and annotated logs.

incident-bot: Incident inc-1965432100 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem scheduled.

maria (pm): tagging for Q3 planning: add AI-715 as "Reliability - KV warmup backoff" to the Q3 epics list.

li (eng-runtime): quick note for the postmortem: include a short simulation script and a reproducer for the KV stampede, so reviewers can test the backoff design. I'll attach it to the RFC.

nate (support): closing loop: I've emailed affected customers with an interim update and promised the technical postmortem + credits where applicable.

samir (oncall): closing the thread for now, will open follow-ups if anything regresses.
